headline: Big 5's Sustainability Winners Point to Refrigerants, Panels and Operations
deck: None of the three Impact Trail awards went to a building. Two went to components and one went to a service contract, which is a fair description of where sustainability money in Gulf construction is actually being spent.
excerpt: The Big 5 Impact Trail named Prime Middle East Trading Company, Masdar and Al-Futtaim Engineering Company as its 2026 winners, for low-GWP refrigerants, wood-based panels and integrated facilities management respectively. The three categories track a shift from headline green buildings towards components and operations that can be measured.
content:
Three awards handed out on the sustainability route through Big 5 Construct Saudi say more about where green spending in Gulf construction is actually going than most of what is printed on the stands. None of the winners is a building. Two are components, and the third is a service contract.

The Big 5 Impact Trail, which runs through the halls at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Conference Center, gave its Sustainability Innovation award to Prime Middle East Trading Company, which trades as PRIMECO, for its Solstice low global warming potential refrigerant range. Best Circular Economy Solution went to Masdar for Kronospan wood-based panels and engineered boards. Al-Futtaim Engineering Company took Operational Sustainability for an integrated facilities management offer.

Take the refrigerant award first, because it is the least glamorous and the most consequential. A chiller is bought once and charged with refrigerant for twenty or thirty years, and the gas inside it is a direct emissions liability for the whole of that period. Solstice is Honeywell's hydrofluoro-olefin family; PRIMECO is an authorised distributor for the region with Riyadh operations. Two of the grades it carries show the range of the problem: R-1234ze is a medium-pressure fluid used in air-cooled and water-cooled chillers for commercial buildings and in heat pumps, while R-1234yf is close to a drop-in replacement for R-134a. Neither changes how a building looks. Both change what its cooling plant is worth in a decade, which in a market building residential, industrial and data-centre capacity at the same time is not a small question.

The circular economy award went to a material rather than a system. Kronospan's wood-based panels and engineered boards were recognised on a carbon-negative basis, which for wood panels rests on the carbon held in the fibre and on how much of that fibre is recovered rather than felled. Panels are a high-volume purchase in fit-out, joinery and furniture packages, and the interesting thing about recognising them is that a specifier does not have to change a design to change the number. The substitution happens inside a line item that was going to be bought anyway.

The third award is the one that points furthest ahead. Al-Futtaim Engineering was recognised for integrated facilities management, which is to say for running buildings rather than making anything that goes into them. Saudi Arabia has spent a decade commissioning assets. The energy those assets consume, the maintenance regime that keeps them efficient and the data that shows whether either is working are a longer revenue stream than the construction that produced them, and the award category is an acknowledgement that the sustainability argument has moved past handover.

The wider trail carried the same logic. Alongside the winners it spotlighted Galaxy Technology, showing Albion Valves with carbon transparency across its cast-iron range; Star Factory, with spray polyurethane foam roofing and waterproofing; and Keller, with ground improvement and foundation work. A valve range with published carbon figures, an insulating roof membrane and a technique that avoids digging out and carting away weak ground are not conceptual. They attach to a purchase order.

Walking the halls this week, the change worth noting is in the questions rather than the answers. The sustainability conversation on the floor has moved from intent to documentation. Buyers want certification that covers the configuration they are actually buying, tested performance rather than brochure performance, lifecycle cost, warranty terms, and evidence that spare parts and technical support exist inside the Kingdom. That is a harder sale than a green claim, and it is a better one.

It also explains the shape of the winners' list. Refrigerant chemistry, panel content and facilities management performance are all measurable at the point of purchase or in an operating contract. A building's sustainability credentials, by contrast, are settled years after the specification is written and by then belong to somebody else. The awards are following the money to where the decision is still reversible.
author: Mo Qureshi
seoTitle: Where Big 5 Saudi's Sustainability Awards Point
seoDescription: PRIMECO, Masdar and Al-Futtaim Engineering took the Big 5 Impact Trail awards for refrigerants, wood panels and integrated facilities management.
